text.p: The following are the reports carried by Estonia's newspapers on Friday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- Estonia should be in the first wave of nations admitted into the European Union, French President Jacques Chirac said at a meeting with President Lennart Meri, visiting Paris.
- The rise of the U.S. dollar on currency markets has raised the prices of electronic equipment in Estonia by 10 percent compared with December.

- Mart Siiman, head of the Coalition Party parliament faction, is also the choice of the Rural Union for new prime minister. Rural Union leader Arnold Ruutel is leading talks on whether to continue with a minority government or extend the coalition.

- The Association of Large Companies wants politicians to pay more attention to the opinion of business but does not intend to interfere in politics, association chairman and head of Hansapank, Hannes Tamjaerv said.
- Parliament intends to amend the law on land registration.
- Sweden is ready to sign a visa-free agreement with Estonia as soon as parliament has ratified the Geneva convention on refugees, Swedish Foreign Minister Lena Hjelm-Wallen said.
- Union Bank forecasts a 1997 profit of 105.8 million kroons and plans to raise the balance sheet total to 7.5 billion kroons.
